observations: Photo 0 shows a black LED moving head light with two hexagonal heads mounted on a central pivot, sitting on a base with a power cable.
Photo 1 shows the unit powered on, emitting purple and red light beams onto a tiled floor.
Photo 2 shows the unit powered on, emitting green laser lines across the floor.
The base in photo 0 has a label with 'LED MOVING HEAD' and a red logo, but the brand name is not legible.

claims.evidence: The label in photo 0 is too blurry to read.

claims.claim: Fully working, recently serviced by the dealer, all parts complete. Original from the manufacturer.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The unit may not power on or the internal electronics may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit powered on and cycling through all modes.

risks.risk: The moving head mechanism may be seized or have mechanical failure.
risks.proof: A video showing the heads rotating and tilting smoothly.

risks.risk: The laser diodes may be burnt out or the laser module may be defective.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the laser module with the unit powered on.

risks.risk: The actual number of LEDs may be different from the claimed 18x10w.
risks.proof: A photo of the LED specification sticker on the back or side of the unit.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the unit powered on and moving through all its light and laser modes.
Photo of the specification sticker on the back of the unit.
Photo of the laser module with the unit powered on.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
